comments.author: @GUAPODELMONTE-YOUTUBE
comments.text:
Nice work Mark, the food is great, the fish broth is great, and the architecture is great, but the Marseille Cathedral "La Mayor" is not based 
on the Hagia Sophia, built by the Catholic, Western, European, Roman Emperor, Constance, hence the City's name CONSTANTINOPLE.
The Cathedral looks much more typical Romanesque, and Gothic. The Cathedral itself, is directly in front of the port, in the middle of
"'the old district" called Le Panier, and the old quarter, was built and frequented by seamen, sailors, merchants and traders from both
Spain and Italy, where they had stayed and helped build the economy of Marseille. A Mediterranean CiTy, and very little to do with the
"Enemy of the Time" - (in the Middle Ages) - Islam and Turkey. Le Panier, used to be called "The Spanish Quarter", until only recently.
It was not called "Little I-stan-bul", or "little Fez", or "little Marrakesh", or "little Rabbat", or "little Atlas". Now it's called "little bread buns".

comments.author: @revelrove
comments.text: Nice video of Marseille! I’m hoping though that going forward that you know that CHEZ is pronounced SHAY.  Also, if you wouldn’t take such huge bites and talk at the same time while you’re chewing, it would make everything much more palatable.  And, if you could use the serving utensils of salads instead of digging in with your own personal utensils, you would be considerate to the other people who are eating. Thank you!
